title: Adjoint of the unbounded proper-open refinement comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $U,V_1,V_2$ be Noetherian schemes, meaning schemes with finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $p:V_1\to V_2$ be proper and let $j_i:U\hookrightarrow V_i$ be open immersions with $pj_1=j_2$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For the commutative square with top $j_1$, bottom $j_2$, left edge $1_U$ and right edge $p$, let
$$b_p:Dj_{2!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*Dj_{1!}$$
be the specific proper/open comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], normalized on a K-injective complex $J$ on $U$ and a K-injective resolution $j_{1!}J\to I$ by $j_{2!}J\cong p_*j_{1!}J\to p_*I$. Here $Dj_{i!}$ means degreewise exact extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Write $\varepsilon_p:p^*Rp_*\to1$ for the counit of exact inverse image and derived direct image [def-kun-unbounded-exchange].
For a module sheaf $M$ on $U$, let $\pi_{p,M}:p^*j_{2!}M\to j_{1!}M$ be the following sheaf map. Put $W=p^{-1}(j_2(U))$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $j_1:U\to W$ is a clopen section of $W\to U$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen]. Under open-extension base change [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], $p^*j_{2!}M$ is extension by zero from $W$ of the pullback of $M$. Define $\pi_{p,M}$ to be its projection onto the component $j_1(U)$, identity there and zero on its complement, using the sheaf decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product]. The construction is natural in $M$ and descends degreewise to $D\pi_p:p^*Dj_{2!}\to Dj_{1!}$. Then the equality of natural transformations on all unbounded complexes is
$$\varepsilon_{p,Dj_{1!}(-)}\circ p^*b_p=D\pi_p.$$
No cartesian condition on the displayed refinement square is assumed.

proof.text: Form $W=V_1\times_{V_2}j_2(U)$ and write $q:W\to U$ for the projection (using the identification of $j_2(U)$ with $U$). The fibre-product universal property gives a section $s=j_1:U\to W$ with $q s=1_U$; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and the definition of open immersion show that this section is open. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $q$ is proper, hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen] gives a disjoint open decomposition $W=s(U)\amalg W^c$. For a module sheaf $M$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product] identifies a sheaf on this binary coproduct with its two components. The inverse of the specified base-change map of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] identifies $p^*j_{2!}M$ with the extension by zero from $W$ of $q^*M$. Define its map to $j_{1!}M$ to be the identity on the $s(U)$ component and zero on $W^c$. This is $\pi_{p,M}$, and the componentwise description proves its naturality in $M$.

proof.text: The inverse-image functor is exact and extension by zero is exact, as recorded in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Applying the natural sheaf map $\pi_{p,-}$ degreewise to an arbitrary unbounded complex gives a chain map $p^*Dj_{2!}K\to Dj_{1!}K$. Exactness makes this construction preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so it descends to the unbounded derived categories and defines $D\pi_p$. The construction is binary and componentwise, hence uses no boundedness or infinite-product assertion.

proof.text:
Let $J$ be a K-injective complex on $U$ and let $\rho:j_{1!}J\to I$ be the chosen K-injective resolution used to normalize $b_p$. The representative clause of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] gives $b_p$ as $j_{2!}J\cong p_*j_{1!}J\xrightarrow{p_*\rho}p_*I$. By [lem-asd-derived-counit-k-injective-termwise], the derived counit at $QI$ is represented, under the canonical comparison, by the ordinary counit $p^*p_*I\to I$. Naturality of that counit along $\rho$ therefore rewrites the composite $p^*j_{2!}J\to p^*p_*I\to I$ as $\psi_J$ followed by $\rho$, where $\psi_J:p^*j_{2!}J\to j_{1!}J$ is the ordinary counit composite obtained from $j_{2!}J=p_*j_{1!}J$.

It remains to identify $\psi_M$ with $\pi_{p,M}$ for a sheaf $M$. Put $W=V_1\times_{V_2}U$, let $w:W\hookrightarrow V_1$ be the open base change and $q:W\to U$ its projection, and let $s=j_1:U\to W$. Outside $W$, both maps vanish by the definition of extension by zero. On $W$, the pullback clause of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], applied to the proper map $p$ and the base change by $j_2$, identifies the restriction of $p_*j_{1!}M$ with $q_*s_*M$; the proper/open specializations and support-composition identification in that same statement identify $j_{2!}M$ with $p_*j_{1!}M$. Thus the restriction of $\psi_M$ is the counit $q^*q_*s_*M\to s_*M$, which is the map $q^*M\to s_*M$ induced by $qs=1_U$. By the clopen decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product], this map is identity on $s(U)$ and zero on the complementary component, exactly the definition of $\pi_{p,M}$. The inverse base-change identification is the $\beta^{-1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], so the calculation is compatible with the Step 1 construction. Hence the representative composite is $\pi_{p,J}$, and naturality in chain maps and resolution independence descend the equality to every unbounded complex.
